Verification passed. Final summary:

## Change

**`src/components/AsyncPanel.tsx`**
- Added an `attempt` counter that the effect now depends on, and a `retryingRef` guard so a retry can only be scheduled once (no overlapping timers; the existing cleanup still clears the timer and a `cancelled` flag also guards the callback).
- On retry: `setState('loading')` renders `Checking service…` immediately, increments `attempt`, and the same 120 ms effect then settles to `success` (the `?sync=error` query only produces the error state on the initial attempt, `attempt === 0`).
- Error state now includes `<button type="button" className="secondary sync-retry">Retry sync</button>` inside the existing `role="alert"` error block. The error state (and hence the button) is only rendered when `state === 'error'`, so it disappears after success and never appears on the success path.
- No page reload, no global/URL mutation, and `AsyncPanel` owns only its own state, so the selected task in `App.tsx` is untouched.

**`src/styles.css`** — added `.sync-retry { justify-self: start; margin-top: 8px; }` reusing the existing `button.secondary` styling.

## Commands run
- `npm run verify:agent` → `tsc --noEmit && vite build` succeeded; `playwright test` → **6 passed** (including the existing "sync success state replaces the loading state").

## Remaining risks
- The `Retry sync` button sits inside the existing `role="alert"` region. Some screen readers may announce the button text as part of the alert; I left the structure unchanged to preserve the existing alert semantics and any existing container-scoped queries.
- Retry deliberately ignores `?sync=error` after the first attempt (always resolves to success) — intended by the spec, but it means the query string no longer reflects the displayed state.
